TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Graph.]
Sour taste after a meal.
Bitter taste in mouth, with sour eructations.
Salty taste.
Taste in mouth as of rotten eggs every morning, which nauseates her.
Tongue coated white.
The tongue after a meal is rough, raw and scraping ; the papillæ are very sensitive, as if they were rubbed against the teeth.
Sore pain on left side of tongue when moving it.
Whitish, painful ulcer on lower surface of tongue.
Burning blisters on lower side and tip of tongue.
Painful vesicles and tubercles on back part of tongue.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Graph.]
Rotten odor from mouth and gums.
Acid, foul odor from mouth.
Breath smells like urine.
Saliva increased, much spitting.
Saliva runs from mouth in morning on stooping.
Dryness of mouth in morning.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Graph.]
Palate : feels sore.
Palate and fauces somewhat reddened. θ Deafness.
Violent catarrh in fauces, with sensation as though food had to pass over a lump in throat ; roughness and rawness in throat ; hoarseness in evening. θ Ozæna scrofulosa.
Swelling of tonsils, with pain when swallowing.
Ulcerative pain in throat.
Roughness and rawness in throat.
Hawking of phlegm ; throat seems full of gurgling mucus.
Sensation on left side of throat as though he had to swallow over an elevation, with scraping in it.
On swallowing sensation of lump in throat, and especially on empty swallowing a constrictive retching from œsophagus up to larynx.
Constant spasm in throat, obliging him to swallow as if he were choking, as if food would not go down.
Constant cramp in throat, causing him to retch, as if the food would not go down.
Nightly pains in throat like a plug, as if the food filled him to the top.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Graph.]
Excessive hunger.
Canine hunger with acidity of stomach.
Appetite excessive or wanting, with much thirst, or with fulness of abdomen.
Violent thirst, early in morning.
Desire for drink to cool one's self internally, without thirst.
Aversion : to animal food, when thinking of it ; to fish ; to cooked food.
Great aversion to salt.
Sweet things are disgusting and nauseous.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Graph.]
Worse when hungry.
Food will not go down.
Pains in stomach necessitate eating.
Is obliged to eat on account of burning in stomach.
Must quickly eat a piece of bread, to > suffocative paroxysm.
Hot things disagree with the stomach.
Abdomen becomes inflated after eating.
